thesis.name: Daily/Weekly Macro-Regime Gold Thesis
thesis.core_statement: Gold directional expectancy should be evaluated as a regime-conditioned daily/weekly system, not as a rescue-filtered intraday candidate stream. Central-bank demand is a slow regime prior; timing is derived from D1/W1 trend, USD/real-yield pressure, ETF-flow divergence, volatility regime, and event-calendar risk.

regime_definitions.description: Central-bank demand regime is supportive, but DXY and real yields are rising; gold thesis requires patience and only high-conviction structural confirmation.
regime_definitions.expected_behavior: trend choppy or capped unless geopolitical/event risk dominates

regime_definitions.description: Central-bank demand supportive while DXY and/or real yields weaken; this is the primary long-thesis regime.
regime_definitions.expected_behavior: trend continuation and pullback-buying should be favored after validation

regime_definitions.description: ETF flows improve while price underperforms or consolidates; potential accumulation/rotation regime, not an immediate timing signal.
regime_definitions.expected_behavior: delayed breakout or regime transition candidate

regime_definitions.description: ETF flows weak or negative while price is extended; continuation quality must be discounted.
regime_definitions.expected_behavior: higher risk of failed breakouts and mean reversion

regime_definitions.description: Major macro/geopolitical/FOMC/CPI/NFP event windows where signal timing must use event-aware validation or remain flat.
